_synthesis_note: Winner: lens C (TWO LINES) supplies the thesis and spine, because the boundary decision is genuinely this case's one idea and it is what makes Ozaukee structural proof rather than a disclaimer. Grafted from lens A (THE DESK): the overheard-question cover, and the seat roster that draws the hiring problem instead of describing it. Grafted from lens B (THE APERTURE): the two line-terminations on the receipts slide, the feathered ramp bar, the redaction slugs, the 30-degree duty dial, and the four-axis pool separation discipline. The 2am staging problem lens A flagged honestly against c33 ('during the day especially') is resolved by making the bright paper slides the daytime register and confining the dark room to the accident-call beat, with NO slide carrying a time-of-day claim.

_ladder_note: SHOWRUNNER DECISION during art build. The akthree climb was planned for S1 (a wide console panel) and was moved to S10 (a macro close-up of three punchdown terminals) after five framing iterations. A wide flat panel read as a sliver at every three-quarter camera and as an unreadable slab head-on. A macro object with three capped terminals is a far simpler thing to frame and is the natural subject for PBR, because chiselled metal caps are exactly what physically based materials are good at. S1 now uses a cabinet-oblique console, which is dimensional rather than flat and which the director had already specified as its designed fallback, so nothing was improvised. render_ladder_top stays akthree.
